payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_session.py::test_a_volume_that_cannot_be_read_either_ends_the_export_once stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/cell/session.py. The claim was "When the volume cannot be read either, `export_patch` returns `None` and the subjects the volume gave, or the cell's when the volume gave none and the cell read them. It does not raise. It writes neither file and emits exactly one `export_failed` teardown line. That line begins `patch export FAILED — ` and names the cell's error, the volume and the volume's own error. The export's network is removed in this case too. The witness drives two such volumes. In one the reader's git fails, and a `commit_subjects` line names the volume. In the other the network create hangs with `runtime.NetworkCreateHung`, and no container starts. When the removal of the cell's container exits non-zero, no container starts either. The one failure line then names the cell's error and the removal's stderr, and the container's name stays in `created`. In that case a cell whose subject read succeeded returns its own subjects. A volume whose subject read succeeds and whose patch read fails returns `(None, subjects)` with those subjects and emits the one failure line. A volume holding no commits past the base emits the base's `no_commits` line, writes neither file and returns `(None, [])`.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
